facts.claim: Section 14A, inserted in the Citizenship Act by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003, lets the Central Government compulsorily register every citizen and issue a national identity card.
facts.quote: (1) The Central Government may compulsorily register every citizen of India and issue national identity card to him.
facts.document: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003 (6 of 2004), section 12 inserting section 14A, as republished in the Mizoram Gazette Extraordinary, Issue No. 178, 3 June 2004
facts.issuer: Parliament of India (republished by the Government of Mizoram)

facts.claim: Section 14A also lets the Central Government maintain a National Register of Indian Citizens, with the Registrar General of India acting as the National Registration Authority.
facts.quote: (2) The Central Government may maintain a National Register of Indian Citizens and for that purpose establish a National Registration Authority.
facts.document: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003 (6 of 2004), new s.14A(2)-(3), as republished in the Mizoram Gazette Extraordinary, Issue No. 178, 3 June 2004
facts.issuer: Parliament of India (republished by the Government of Mizoram)

facts.claim: The Ministry of Home Affairs told the Lok Sabha that section 14A came into force on 3 December 2004.
facts.quote: Section 14A prescribing compulsory registration of every citizen of India, was inserted in the Citizenship Act, 1955 w.e.f. 03.12.2004.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 2476, 'Updation of NPR', answered 3 December 2019

facts.claim: The Citizenship (Registration of Citizens and Issue of National Identity Cards) Rules, 2003 were notified on 10 December 2003 as G.S.R. 937(E) under section 18 of the Citizenship Act.
facts.quote: G.S.R.937(E).- In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-sections (1) and (3) of section 18 of the Citizenship Act, 1955 (57 of 1955), the Central Government hereby makes the following rules
facts.document: Citizenship (Registration of Citizens and Issue of National Identity Cards) Rules, 2003, notification G.S.R. 937(E), 10 December 2003 (MHA copy)

facts.claim: The 2003 Rules define the National Register of Indian Citizens as a register of the details of Indian citizens living in India and abroad.
facts.quote: “National Register of Indian Citizens” means the register containing details of Indian Citizens living in India and outside India;
facts.document: Citizenship Rules, 2003, rule 2(k)

facts.claim: The 2003 Rules define the Population Register as a register of persons usually resident in a local area, without any reference to citizenship.
facts.quote: “Population Register” means the register containing details of persons usually residing in a village or rural area or town or ward or demarcated area
facts.document: Citizenship Rules, 2003, rule 2(l)

facts.claim: Under rule 3, the Registrar General of Citizen Registration is to establish and maintain the National Register of Indian Citizens.
facts.quote: (1) The Registrar General of Citizen Registration shall establish and maintain the National Register of Indian Citizens.
facts.document: Citizenship Rules, 2003, rule 3(1)

facts.claim: Rule 3(4) lets the Central Government decide a date for preparing the Population Register of everyone usually resident. Rule 3(5) says the local register of citizens is drawn from it after verification.
facts.quote: (4) The Central Government may, by an order issued in this regard, decide a date by which the Population Register shall be prepared by collecting information relating to all persons who are usually residing within the jurisdiction of Local Registrar. (5) The Local Register of Indian citizens shall contain details of persons after due verification made from the Population Register.
facts.document: Citizenship Rules, 2003, rule 3(4)-(5)

facts.claim: Rule 4 provides for a house-to-house enumeration across the country, including citizenship status, to prepare the national register.
facts.quote: The Central Government shall, for the purpose of National Register of Indian Citizens, cause to carry throughout the country a house-to-house enumeration for collection of specified particulars relating to each family and individual, residing in a local area including the Citizenship status.
facts.document: Citizenship Rules, 2003, rule 4(1)

facts.claim: Under rule 4(4), people whose citizenship is doubtful are to be marked in the Population Register for further enquiry and told so. Rule 4(5) gives them a hearing before a decision.
facts.quote: During the verification process, particulars of such individuals, whose Citizenship is doubtful, shall be entered by the Local Registrar with appropriate remark in the Population Register for further enquiry
facts.document: Citizenship Rules, 2003, rule 4(4)-(5)

facts.claim: Rule 6 says the Registrar General is to notify, by order, the date on which the National Register of Indian Citizens is initialised throughout the country.
facts.quote: The Registrar General of Citizen Registration shall, by order, notify the date on which the National Register of Indian Citizens shall be initialized throughout the country.
facts.document: Citizenship Rules, 2003, rule 6(1)

facts.claim: Rule 4A, added in November 2009, takes Assam out of rule 4 and has the register in Assam prepared by inviting applications from all residents, based on the 1951 NRC and the electoral rolls up to midnight of 24 March 1971.
facts.quote: (1) Nothing in rule 4 shall, on and after the commencement of the Citizenship (Registration of Citizenship and Issue of National Identity Cards) Amendment Rules, 2009, apply to the State of Assam.
facts.document: In Re: Section 6A of the Citizenship Act 1955, W.P.(C) 274/2009, judgment of 17 October 2024 (2024 INSC 789), opinion of Chandrachud CJI, para 106 and footnotes 190-191 (rule 4A reproduced)

facts.claim: Rule 4A(4) says the manner of preparing the register in Assam is set out in a Schedule to the 2003 Rules.
facts.quote: (4) The manner of preparation of the National Register of Indian Citizens in the State of Assam shall be such as specified in the Schedule appended to these rules.
facts.document: In Re: Section 6A, judgment of 17 October 2024, opinion of Chandrachud CJI, fn 191 (rule 4A reproduced)

facts.claim: In the Section 6A judgment, Chief Justice Chandrachud's opinion summarised the Schedule for Assam. The 1951 NRC and the electoral rolls up to midnight of 24 March 1971 are published, residents apply, and a consolidated list is made of those on those records and their descendants, leaving out anyone declared an illegal migrant or a foreigner.
facts.quote: The Local Registrar of Citizen Registration must scrutinize all the applications and prepare a consolidated list which must contain the names of (i) persons who appear in electoral rolls prior to the year 1971 or NCR 1951, and (ii) their descendants
facts.document: In Re: Section 6A, judgment of 17 October 2024, opinion of Chandrachud CJI, para 107

facts.claim: The Ministry of Home Affairs told the Lok Sabha that the Assam update was carried out under the Citizenship Act and the Schedule framed under rule 4A(4) of the 2003 Rules, under the Supreme Court's supervision.
facts.quote: The updation of the National Register of Citizens (NRC) in the State of Assam has been undertaken as per the provisions of the Citizenship Act,1955 and the provisions contained in the Schedule framed under Rule 4A (4) of the Citizenship (Registration of Citizens and Issue of National Identity Cards) Rules, 2003.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 2072, 'Updation of NRC', answered 14 March 2023

facts.claim: A National Register of Citizens was prepared for Assam in 1951.
facts.quote: The Central Government prepared the National Register of Citizens in Assam in 1951 which consisted of information on all the citizens in Assam.
facts.document: In Re: Section 6A, judgment of 17 October 2024, opinion of Chandrachud CJI, para 105

facts.claim: Clause 5.8 of the Assam Accord of 15 August 1985 provides that foreigners who came to Assam on or after 25 March 1971 are to continue to be detected, deleted and expelled in accordance with law.
facts.quote: 5.8 Foreigners who came to Assam on or after March 25, 1971 shall continue to be detected, deleted and expelled in accordance with the law.
facts.document: In Re: Section 6A, judgment of 17 October 2024, opinion of J.B. Pardiwala J, para 73, the Memorandum of Settlement reproduced

facts.claim: Section 6A, added in 1985, deems people of Indian origin who came to Assam from the territory now in Bangladesh before 1 January 1966, and have lived there ordinarily since, to be citizens from that date. Those who came between 1 January 1966 and 24 March 1971 and are detected to be foreigners must register, cannot be on an electoral roll for ten years from detection, and are deemed citizens after those ten years.
facts.quote: (2) Subject to the provisions of sub-sections (6) and (7), all persons of Indian origin who came before the 1st day of January, 1966 to Assam from the specified territory ... shall be deemed to be citizens of India as from the 1st day of January, 1966.
facts.document: In Re: Section 6A, judgment of 17 October 2024, opinion of Chandrachud CJI, fn 3 (s.6A reproduced)

facts.claim: On 17 October 2024 a five-judge bench upheld section 6A by majority, with one judge dissenting.
facts.quote: In terms of the majority opinion, the writ petitions are disposed of.
facts.document: Record of proceedings, W.P.(C) 274/2009 In Re: Section 6A of the Citizenship Act 1955 and connected, 17 October 2024

facts.claim: The majority held that people who entered Assam on or after 25 March 1971 are not covered by section 6A.
facts.quote: immigrants who entered the State of Assam on or after 25.03.1971 are not entitled to the protection conferred vide Section 6A
facts.document: Record of proceedings, 17 October 2024, quoting para 391(b) of the opinion of Surya Kant J

facts.claim: The Supreme Court records that the first petition, filed in 2009 by Assam Public Works, sought updating of the 1951 NRC, and that a two-judge bench then began monitoring the NRC update.
facts.quote: Following this, a 2-judge bench of this court started monitoring the NRC updation process.
facts.document: In Re: Section 6A, judgment of 17 October 2024, opinion of Surya Kant J, para 28

facts.claim: A part draft NRC of 1.9 crore of the 3.29 crore applicants was published on 31 December 2017, as the Supreme Court recorded from the State Coordinator's report.
facts.quote: The Part Draft NRC comprising 1.9 crore applicants out of the total 3.29 crore applicants were published on 31st December, 2017.
facts.document: Record of proceedings, W.P.(C) 274/2009 Assam Public Works v Union of India, 2 July 2018 (quoting para 10 of the State Coordinator's report)

facts.claim: The complete draft NRC was published on 30 July 2018 with 2,89,83,677 people included, as recorded by the Supreme Court the next day.
facts.quote: Complete Draft NRC was published on 30th July, 2018 and the total number of persons included in the said Complete Draft NRC is 2,89,83,677 leaving a total of 40,70,707 as ineligible for inclusion.
facts.document: Record of proceedings, W.P.(C) 274/2009 Assam Public Works v Union of India, 31 July 2018

facts.claim: Of the names left out of the complete draft, 37,59,630 were rejected and 2,48,077 kept on hold, according to the same order.
facts.quote: Out of the aforesaid 40,70,707 names, 37,59,630 names have been rejected and 2,48,077 names were kept on hold.
facts.document: Record of proceedings, Assam Public Works v Union of India, 31 July 2018

facts.claim: The Court said the complete draft could not be the basis of action by any authority.
facts.quote: what has been published is only the Complete Draft NRC which naturally being a draft cannot be the basis of any action by any authority.
facts.document: Record of proceedings, Assam Public Works v Union of India, 31 July 2018

facts.claim: The Ministry of Home Affairs told the Lok Sabha that the complete draft was published on 30 July 2018 and that the supplementary list of inclusions and the list of exclusions were published on 31 August 2019.
facts.quote: On the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court, the Complete Draft NRC, Assam was published on 30th July, 2018 and the supplementary list of inclusions and the list of exclusions have been published on 31st August, 2019.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 2627, 'Appeal to Foreigners Tribunal', answered 14 December 2021

facts.claim: On 31 August 2019, 3,11,21,004 people were found eligible for inclusion and 19,06,657 were left out.
facts.quote: A total of 3,11,21,004 persons are found eligible for inclusion leaving out 19,06,657 persons.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 3448, 'NRC in Assam', answered 16 March 2021

facts.claim: The Ministry described the Assam NRC as application based, with each applicant required to prove residence of self or an ancestor in India on or before the cut-off date through a listed legacy document.
facts.quote: NRC in Assam is an application based process. Each applicant is mandatorily required to furnish a documentary proof of residence of self or the ancestors (legacy person) in Assam or any other part of India on or before the cut-off date, through one of the stipulated legacy documents.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 1264, 'NRC in Assam', answered 9 February 2021

facts.claim: The decision on eligibility of 'D' voters and their descendants was kept on hold on the Supreme Court's direction.
facts.quote: The decision of eligibility of ‘D’ Voters and their descendants has been kept on hold on the direction of Hon’ble Supreme Court.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 3448, answered 16 March 2021

facts.claim: The Supreme Court directed that the lists be made available to the State, the Centre and the Registrar General only after a security regime like Aadhaar's was put in place.
facts.quote: The Hon’ble Supreme Court has directed the State Coordinator to enact an appropriate security regime on lines similar to the security regime provided for AADHAR data and only thereafter the list of inclusions and exclusions shall be made available to the State Government, Central Government and Registrar General India.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Starred Question No. 14, 'National Register of Citizens', answered 2 February 2021

facts.claim: As of March 2021 the Government said the final NRC in Assam had not been issued, so no certified rejection orders had gone out and no appeals had been filed.
facts.quote: However, the final National Register of Indian Citizens (NRC) in Assam has not been issued. Consequently, certified copy of the rejection order has not been issued to the persons excluded from the final NRC. Hence, the number of appeals made to the Foreigners Tribunal by those excluded from the final NRC list is ‘Nil’ as on date.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 4425, 'Appeals made to Foreigners Tribunals', answered 23 March 2021

facts.claim: Rejection slips were postponed because of Covid-19 and floods.
facts.quote: Due to outbreak of Covid-19 and flood situation, the process of issuing rejection slips has been postponed.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Starred Question No. 111, 'National Register of Citizens in Assam', answered 27 July 2021

facts.claim: The latest primary statement found on rejection orders, from December 2021, says the State Coordinator had not yet issued them.
facts.quote: The State Coordinator, NRC Assam has not yet issued rejection orders against which appeals may be preferred to the Foreigners Tribunal.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 2627, 'Appeal to Foreigners Tribunal', answered 14 December 2021

facts.claim: Anyone dissatisfied with a decision on claims and objections may appeal to a Foreigners Tribunal within 120 days, extended from 60 days with effect from 21 August 2019.
facts.quote: The period of appeal has been increased from ‘Sixty days’ to ‘One hundred and twenty days’ for preferring appeal before the designated Tribunal with effect from 21st August, 2019.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 1264, answered 9 February 2021

facts.claim: Since those excluded had not exhausted their legal remedies, the Government said nationality verification did not arise at that stage.
facts.quote: Since persons excluded from the NRC in Assam have not yet exhausted all possible legal remedies, the question of nationality verification of such persons does not arise at this stage.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 3451, 'Persons excluded from NRC', answered 10 August 2021

facts.claim: The Supreme Court declined, on 23 July 2019, a request by the Union and the State for a sample re-verification of the NRC, as the Ministry later told the Lok Sabha.
facts.quote: Taking note of the prayers made on behalf of the Union of India and the State of Assam for a sample re-verification of a limited percentage of the exercise done to take care of wrongful inclusions and exclusions, Hon’ble Supreme Court did not consider it necessary to accede to the prayers while hearing the matter on 23.07.2019
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 1932, 'Review of NRC', answered 3 March 2020

facts.claim: The approved cost of updating the 1951 NRC in Assam was Rs 1,602.66 crore, of which Rs 1,602.52 crore had been released.
facts.quote: The approved cost of the scheme of Updation of National Register of Citizens (NRC), 1951 in Assam is Rs.1602.66 crore, out of which Rs.1602.52 crore has been released to the Government of Assam.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 2624, 'NRC List', answered 14 December 2021

facts.claim: The National Population Register was first prepared in 2010 and updated in 2015, under rule 3(4) of the 2003 Rules.
facts.quote: In pursuance of sub rule (4) of rule 3 of the Citizenship (Registration of Citizens and Issue of National Identity Card) Rules, 2003, framed under the Citizenship Act, 1955, the Central Government prepared National Population Register in 2010 and updated it in 2015.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 2476, 'Updation of NPR', answered 3 December 2019

facts.claim: On 31 July 2019 the Central Government notified that the Population Register would be prepared and updated, house to house, across the country except Assam, between 1 April and 30 September 2020.
facts.quote: the Central Government hereby decides to prepare and update the Population Register and the field work for house to house enumeration throughout the country except Assam for collection of information relating to all persons who are usually residing within the jurisdiction of Local Registrar shall be undertaken between the 1st day of April, 2020 to 30th September, 2020.
facts.document: Notification S.O. 2753(E), Gazette of India Extraordinary No. 2503, Part II Sec. 3(ii), 31 July 2019
facts.issuer: Ministry of Home Affairs (Office of the Registrar General Citizen Registration, India)

facts.claim: The Government planned to update the NPR alongside the houselisting phase of Census 2021 and estimated Rs 3,941.35 crore for it.
facts.quote: It has been estimated that an amount of Rs. 8754.23 crore for conducting Census 2021 and Rs. 3941.35 crore for updating National Population Register would be required.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 2476, answered 3 December 2019

facts.claim: The Government said no document was to be collected during the NPR update and that Aadhaar would be collected voluntarily.
facts.quote: No document is to be collected during the updation of NPR.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 387, 'Updation of NPR', answered 4 February 2020
facts.where: answer (e) & (f); answer (a): 'Aadhaar number is collected voluntarily.'

facts.claim: The Government said no verification to find people of doubtful citizenship is done while updating the NPR.
facts.quote: During the exercise of updation of National Population Register (NPR), no verification is done to find individuals whose citizenship is doubtful.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 376, 'Preparation of NPR', answered 4 February 2020

facts.claim: The NPR update and Census 2021 field work were postponed until further orders because of Covid-19.
facts.quote: However, due to outbreak of COVID-19 pandemic, the conduct of Census 2021, updating of National Population Register and the related field activities have been postponed until further orders.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 1016, 'National Population Register', answered 8 February 2022

facts.claim: The Government notified its intent to hold the Census on 16 June 2025, in two phases, with reference date 1 March 2027 (1 October 2026 for Ladakh, snow-bound parts of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand).
facts.quote: The Government of India has notified its intent to conduct Census in the Gazette on 16th June,2025. The Census will be conducted in two phases.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 1382, 'Population Census-2027', answered 29 July 2025

facts.claim: The latest primary statement found on the NPR says no decision has been taken to update it.
facts.quote: No decision has been taken to update the National Population Register.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 1382, 'Population Census-2027', answered 29 July 2025

facts.claim: Houselisting for Census 2027 was set for April to September 2026, in a 30-day window chosen by each State, with population enumeration in February 2027.
facts.quote: The Census 2027 will be conducted in two phases namely Phase I – House Listing and Housing Census from April to September, 2026 in a period of 30 days as per the convenience of the State/UT Governments followed by Phase II – Population Enumeration (PE).
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 258, 'Resumption of Census 2021', answered 2 December 2025

facts.claim: Asked whether census data would be linked with the NPR or voter rolls, the Ministry said individual census data is kept confidential and only aggregates are published.
facts.quote: Individual data collected in the Census is kept confidential and only aggregated data at various administrative levels is published.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 5278, 'Census 2027 Safeguards', answered 24 March 2026

facts.claim: On 2020-02-04, the Ministry of Home Affairs told the Lok Sabha that no decision had been taken to prepare a National Register of Indian Citizens at the national level.
facts.quote: Till now, the Government has not taken any decision to prepare National Register of Indian Citizens (NRIC) at the National level.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Starred Question No. 22, 'National Register of Citizens', answered 4 February 2020

facts.claim: On 2020-02-04, the Ministry of Home Affairs told the Lok Sabha that no decision had been taken to prepare a National Register of Indian Citizens at the national level.
facts.quote: Till now, the Government has not taken any decision to prepare National Register of Indian Citizens (NRIC) at the National level.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 425, 'Keeping NPR on Hold', answered 4 February 2020

facts.claim: On 2021-08-10, the Ministry of Home Affairs told the Lok Sabha that no decision had been taken to prepare a National Register of Indian Citizens at the national level.
facts.quote: Till Now, the Government has not taken any decision to prepare National Register of Indian Citizens (NRIC) at National Level.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 3455, 'Status of CAA, NRC and NPR', answered 10 August 2021

facts.claim: On 2021-12-14, the Ministry of Home Affairs told the Lok Sabha that no decision had been taken to prepare a National Register of Indian Citizens at the national level.
facts.quote: Till now, the Government has not taken any decision to prepare National Register of Indian Citizens (NRIC) at the National level.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 2627, 'Appeal to Foreigners Tribunal', answered 14 December 2021

facts.claim: On 2023-03-21, the Ministry of Home Affairs told the Lok Sabha that no decision had been taken to prepare a National Register of Indian Citizens at the national level.
facts.quote: Till Now, the Government has not taken any decision to prepare National Register of Indian Citizens (NRIC) at National Level.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 3389, 'Update on NRC, CAA and NPR', answered 21 March 2023

facts.claim: The Ministry said that rule 6 of the 2003 Rules, under which the national register is initialised, does not contradict rule 4.
facts.quote: Rule 6 of the Citizenship (Registration of Citizens and Issue of National Identity Cards) Rules, 2003 does not contradict Rule 4.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 376, 'Preparation of NPR', answered 4 February 2020

facts.claim: The Commission ordered the Bihar SIR under Article 324 and section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
facts.quote: the Commission has directed a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in exercise of its powers under Article 324, Section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 (the “RPA 1950”), along with other applicable provisions of the RPA 1950
facts.document: ECI letter No. 23/2025-ERS (Vol.II) dated 24 June 2025 to the CEO, Bihar (Annexure I to the order of 27 October 2025), copy hosted by CEO Kerala

facts.claim: The order made each Electoral Registration Officer responsible for enrolling every eligible person, as Article 326 read with sections 16 and 19 of the Representation of the People Act requires, and for being satisfied of each person's eligibility.
facts.quote: During the SIR, CEO/DEO will aid ERO to fulfil the constitutional mandate that every eligible person, as per Article 326 of the Constitution of India read with Section 16 and 19 of the RPA 1950, is enrolled as Elector.
facts.document: ECI letter No. 23/2025-ERS (Vol.II) dated 24 June 2025 to the CEO, Bihar

facts.claim: The SIR order of 24 June 2025 says Article 326 requires a person to be an Indian citizen to be registered in the electoral roll, and that consequently the Commission has 'a constitutional obligation to ensure that only persons who are citizens' (the sentence breaks off there as printed).
facts.quote: Whereas, one of the fundamental pre-conditions set out in Article 326 of the Constitution is that a person is required to be an Indian citizen, for his/her name to be registered in the electoral roll. Consequently, the Commission has a constitutional obligation to ensure that only persons who are citizens;
facts.document: ECI Order No. 23/ERS/2025 dated 24 June 2025, 'Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls' (Annexure A)

facts.claim: The order treats the 2003 Bihar roll as probative evidence of eligibility including a presumption of citizenship, and requires people not on it to submit documents.
facts.quote: the EROs shall treat the electoral roll of 2003 with qualifying date of 01.01.2003 as probative evidence of eligibility, including presumption of citizenship unless they receive any other input otherwise.
facts.document: ECI Order No. 23/ERS/2025 dated 24 June 2025 (Annexure A)

facts.claim: Phase II of the SIR, ordered on 27 October 2025, again cites Article 324 and section 21, and says no document is to be collected during enumeration.
facts.quote: No document is to be collected from electors during the Enumeration Phase.
facts.document: ECI letter No. 23/2025-ERS (Vol.II) dated 27 October 2025 to the CEOs of twelve States and UTs, copy hosted by CEO Kerala

facts.claim: The SIR's list of documents for phase II, which it calls indicative and not exhaustive, has 13 items. The National Register of Citizens, 'wherever it exists', is item 9. Eleven items are kinds of document, one is the Aadhaar directions of 9 September 2025, and one is an extract of Bihar's SIR roll.
facts.quote: 9. National Register of Citizens (wherever it exists)
facts.document: Information sheet to the Enumeration Form, Annexure III to ECI letter of 27 October 2025

facts.claim: The Supreme Court directed that Aadhaar be accepted as proof of identity, as a twelfth document, for inclusion in or exclusion from Bihar's revised roll, while recording that it is not proof of citizenship.
facts.quote: it is not a proof of citizenship and therefore shall not be accepted as proof of citizenship. However, keeping in view Section 23(4) of the Representation of People Act, 1950, the Aadhaar Card is one of the documents enumerated for the purpose of establishing the identity of a person.
facts.document: Record of proceedings, W.P.(C) 640/2025 Association for Democratic Reforms v Election Commission of India and connected, 8 September 2025

facts.claim: Before the Court, counsel for the Commission argued that its exercise was an enquiry into eligibility for enrolment and did not determine anyone's citizenship.
facts.quote: Even otherwise, the Commission's exercise in the present case is not a determination of citizenship per se but an enquiry into eligibility for enrolment, which is a function squarely within its constitutional remit.
facts.document: ADR v ECI, W.P.(C) 640/2025, judgment of 27 May 2026 (2026 INSC 564), submissions for the Election Commission as recorded, para 14(r)
facts.issuer: Supreme Court of India (recording the ECI's submission)

facts.claim: The Supreme Court held the SIR to be traceable to section 21(3) of the RP Act read with Article 324.
facts.quote: It is, instead, an exercise traceable to Section 21(3) of the RP Act read with Article 324 of the Constitution
facts.document: ADR v ECI, judgment of 27 May 2026, para 186(a)

facts.claim: The Court held that formal determination of citizenship belongs exclusively to the competent authority under the Citizenship Act and cannot be undertaken by the Commission.
facts.quote: the formal determination of citizenship, particularly where it entails adjudication of status or deprivation thereof, falls within the exclusive domain of the Competent Authority under the Citizenship Act. There can be no dispute that such a determination cannot be undertaken by the Commission
facts.document: ADR v ECI, judgment of 27 May 2026, para 171

facts.claim: The Court held the Commission may make a limited enquiry into citizenship for enrolment, which is not a determination of citizenship and has electoral consequences only.
facts.quote: The Commission is empowered, in the exercise of its constitutional mandate, to undertake a limited enquiry into citizenship for the purpose of satisfying itself as to eligibility for inclusion in the electoral roll. Such an enquiry does not amount to a determination of citizenship in the strict sense, and any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone.
facts.document: ADR v ECI, judgment of 27 May 2026, para 186(f)

facts.claim: The Court said that declining to enrol someone does not declare that person not to be a citizen.
facts.quote: It does not amount to a declaration that the individual is not a citizen of India; it merely reflects the Commission’s inability to be satisfied, for electoral purposes, that the statutory conditions are met.
facts.document: ADR v ECI, judgment of 27 May 2026, para 176

facts.claim: Where the Commission is not satisfied, it must refer the person to the competent authority of the Central Government, and any deletion on that ground stays subject to that authority's decision.
facts.quote: In cases where the Commission is not satisfied that a person meets the statutory conditions for inclusion in the electoral roll, it would be incumbent upon it to refer such an individual to the competent authority within the Central Government for adjudication in accordance with law.
facts.document: ADR v ECI, judgment of 27 May 2026, para 186(g)

facts.claim: The Court upheld the SIR's documentation regime, with Aadhaar included by its order of 8 September 2025.
facts.quote: The classification of documents, including the exclusion of certain categories (apart from Aadhar Card, which was directed to be included vide Order dated 08.09.2025), is based on intelligible criteria having a direct nexus with the objective of ensuring the integrity of the electoral roll.
facts.document: ADR v ECI, judgment of 27 May 2026, para 186(e)

facts.claim: The Law Ministry told the Lok Sabha in July 2026 that the SIR is being carried out in phases and that the Court found it within the Commission's mandate under the RP Act and Article 324.
facts.quote: the SIR exercise is within the statutory mandate of ECI under the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and is consonance with the Election Commission's constitutional obligation under Article 324 to ensure free and fair elections.
facts.document: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 990, 'SIR Electoral Roll Revision', answered 24 July 2026
facts.issuer: Ministry of Law and Justice (Legislative Department)

facts.claim: Assam's revision was a Special Revision under section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, with 1 January 2026 as the qualifying date. It was ordered separately from the Special Intensive Revision.
facts.quote: the Commission has directed a Special Revision (SR) u/s 21 of the Representation of the Peoples Act 1950, with reference to 01.01.2026 as the qualifying date, in the State of Assam.
facts.document: ECI letter No. 23/2025-ERS (Vol. II) dated 17 November 2025 to the CEO, Assam, 'Special Revision w.r.t. 01.01.2026 as the qualifying date'

facts.claim: In Assam, booth level officers checked a printed register of the electors already on the roll, house by house. The order names no enumeration form.
facts.quote: For field verification, the BLOs will be given a pre-filled BLO register (Statement-1) containing the details of existing electors in their respective part for H2H field visit.
facts.document: ECI letter of 17 November 2025 to the CEO, Assam

facts.claim: D-voters were left out of the verification register and carried onto the draft unchanged, to be altered only on a Foreigners Tribunal or court order.
facts.quote: Any modification, including removal or deletion, shall be made only upon receipt of an order from the competent Foreigners’ Tribunal or an appropriate court of law.
facts.document: ECI letter of 17 November 2025 to the CEO, Assam

facts.claim: The Assam order cites the same rule on who may be enrolled as the SIR does, Article 326 with sections 16 and 19 of the Representation of the People Act.
facts.quote: During the SR, CEO/DEO/ERO will ensure that every eligible person, as per Article 326 of the Constitution of India and Section 16 and 19 of the Representative of Peoples Act, 1950, is enrolled as Elector.
facts.document: ECI letter of 17 November 2025 to the CEO, Assam

facts.claim: Aadhaar was voluntary on Form 6 and Form 8 in the Assam revision, and no entry could be deleted for not giving it.
facts.quote: However, no application for inclusion of name in electoral roll shall be denied and no entries in electoral roll shall be deleted for inability of an individual to furnish or intimate Aadhaar Number.
facts.document: ECI letter of 17 November 2025 to the CEO, Assam

facts.claim: The Assam Special Revision order does not mention the National Register of Citizens.
facts.document: ECI letter of 17 November 2025 to the CEO, Assam, all 18 pages of the letter

reported.claim: The NRC State Coordinator's office said 3,30,27,661 people had applied, of whom 3,11,21,004 were included and 19,06,657 excluded.

unsettled: The number who applied to Assam's NRC. The 3,30,27,661 in the press is the State Coordinator's figure as reported, and equals those found eligible and those left out added together. The Supreme Court's orders give only 3.29 crore.

How many were left out of the complete draft of 30 July 2018. The Supreme Court's order of 31 July 2018 prints 40,70,707, but its own split, 37,59,630 rejected and 2,48,077 on hold, adds to 40,07,707. Only the second agrees with 3.29 crore applicants. This page gives the two parts and no total.
The date of the final list. Every answer of the Ministry gives 31 August 2019. One opinion in the Supreme Court's judgment of 17 October 2024 gives 13 August 2019. This page uses 31 August 2019.
Whether the Registrar General has notified the final NRC for Assam. No document found says it has. In March 2021 the Ministry said the final NRC had not been issued.
Whether rejection orders have gone out since December 2021, when the Ministry said they had not.

Any statement by the Government in Parliament on a nationwide NRC after 21 March 2023, or on updating the NPR after 29 July 2025. The Lok Sabha's answers were searched to October 2026, and the Rajya Sabha's were not searched in full.
An order or press note in which the Election Commission says in its own words how the SIR relates to the NRC. Its position is known from its counsel's submissions as the Supreme Court recorded them.
The Supreme Court's monitoring orders on the NRC of 2013 and 2014, and of 23 July and 13 August 2019, which could not be found.
